Maya’s breath hitched, trailing white mist into the freezing air. The brass pocket watch felt alive in her palm, pulsing with a rhythmic warmth that defied the sub-zero cold. She looked up, searching the glowing amber eyes behind the heavy glass visor. 

Slowly, the weightless figure reached up. With a hiss of depressurization, he unlatched the antique brass helmet and lifted it away. 

Dark curls tumbled free, dusted with frost, framing a face that was strikingly handsome—and impossibly familiar. He had sharp cheekbones, a soft smile, and eyes that held the starlight of a hundred forgotten nights. 

"Julian?" Maya whispered, the name escaping her lips before her mind could fully process it. He was the lost engineer from the 1890 expedition, the man whose worn journal she had read by lamplight every night since arriving at the station. 

"I waited a long time, Maya," Julian said, his voice like velvet over gravel, wrapping around her like a warm blanket. He stepped closer, hovering just inches above the metal gantry. His fingers brushed her frozen cheek, radiating a heat that instantly thawed the ice on her skin. "The storm caught me all those years ago, but the warmth of your spirit kept my soul anchored here."

Her heart hammered against her ribs, a wild, impossible surge of emotion flooding through her. Romance had been the last thing on her mind at the edge of the world, but as his thumb gently traced her jawline, the vast, empty Arctic vanished. There was only him.

"How is this possible?" she breathed, leaning into his touch.

Julian gently pressed her hand, closing her fingers around the pocket watch. "Love bends time, my sun-repairer. But the tower's core is awakening, and our time is running short."

Beneath their feet, the steel platform groaned softly as a deep, brilliant violet light flared from the abyss below, beginning to pull him backward into the mist.

Come back for the next part tomorrow.
